request: QA lead 14 Oct 2026: sheet of only the cases whose expected behaviour changed since 22 Sep; columns expected before / now, steps before / now, with dates.
method: Behaviour-first over all 91 cases. A case is included only when its steps perform a scenario whose expected behaviour changed in PRD v43 or a later winning Jira decision, and following the case today would fail a correct build or pass a build that still behaves the old way. Before-columns are verbatim from the live case (checked by script); now-columns follow the current spec or decision.

cases.case_title: Choose which work order gets the lines, or a new one, before drafting
cases.why: For a work order that cannot take lines, the menu now still opens and offers only a new work order, instead of creating one without asking or listing the old work order with a reason.
steps_before: 3. On the ineligible-work-order inspection, confirm a new work order is created without asking, for the same customer and asset.
4. Confirm an ineligible destination keeps its place in the menu and states why.
expected_before: When the run-on work order is not eligible (Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, or an invoice already exists), a new work order is created without asking.
A destination that cannot take lines keeps its place in the menu and says why, rather than silently disappearing.
expected_now: On the inspection whose work order is not eligible (Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, or it already has an invoice), pressing Build lines still opens the destination menu; no new work order is created without asking.
The menu offers only a new work order. The inspection's own work order is not listed at all: it is not shown greyed out and no reason is given.
Choosing the new work order creates it for the same customer and asset and the drafting starts there.
steps_now: 1. Open the completed inspection whose work order is not eligible (for example Complete, or already invoiced).
2. Press Build lines.
3. Read the destination menu that opens.
4. Check the inspection's own work order is not in the menu and only a new work order is offered.
5. Choose the new work order.
6. Check a new work order is created for the same customer and asset and the drafting starts on it.

cases.case_title: After building you land on Lines, the finding is marked done, rebuild asks
cases.why: Lines can now be built from an inspection only once: a second set is never added and no confirmation is asked.
steps_before: 4. Press Add Lines a second time from the same inspection; confirm you are asked to confirm before a second set is added.
expected_before: If lines were already added from this inspection, the user is asked to confirm before adding a second set, checked when Add Lines is pressed.
expected_now: An inspection is built from once. After its lines have been added, the completed inspection, the work order note and the asset's Inspections tab row no longer offer Build lines; each shows the outcome instead ('WO created …' or 'Lines added …') with a link to the work order that got the lines.
If a second set of proposed lines was already open for the same inspection, pressing Add Lines there adds nothing and tells you where the lines went.
No question asking you to confirm a second set appears at any point.
steps_now: 1. Open the same completed inspection in two browser tabs.
2. In the first tab, press Build lines, choose a target and wait for the proposed lines.
3. In the second tab, press Build lines, choose a target and wait for the proposed lines.
4. In the first tab, press Add Lines.
5. In the second tab, press Add Lines.
6. Check nothing is added from the second tab and a message says where the lines went.
7. Open the completed inspection, the work order's inspection note and the asset's Inspections tab row.
8. Check none of them offers Build lines and each shows the outcome with a link to the work order that got the lines.

cases.case_title: Building lines with long notes, many findings, or a deleted work order
cases.why: A second Add Lines no longer adds a duplicate set, and after the run-on work order is deleted the inspection no longer goes back to needing a work order.
steps_before: 4. Repeat, using the second browser to reopen the inspection, and to delete the built lines versus delete the work order; check each result against the expected result below.
expected_before: If two users draft from the same inspection at once, the drafting itself duplicates nothing; duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable.

If the run-on work order is deleted, the inspection survives it and stays listed on the asset with a dash in its work order column; any lines added to that work order are gone with it and the inspection counts as needing a work order again.
expected_now: If two users draft from the same inspection at once, the drafting duplicates nothing. When both press Add Lines, only the first adds lines; the second adds nothing and is told where the lines went.

If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted, a completed inspection (one that has a report) stays listed on the asset's Inspections tab as a read-only record with a dash in the Work order column. An inspection with no report is deleted with the work order.
Lines that had been added to the deleted work order are gone with it.
The inspection does not count as needing a work order again: it offers no Build lines and is not counted in the summary line, because it can no longer be built from.
steps_now: 1. Build from a completed inspection, choose the work order it was run on, and press Add Lines.
2. In the second browser, delete that work order.
3. Open the asset's Inspections tab and find the inspection.
4. Check it is still listed, with a dash in the Work order column and no Build lines.
5. Check it is not counted in the summary line 'N of M have findings with no lines yet'.
6. In both browsers, open Build lines on another completed inspection with findings and wait for the proposed lines.
7. Press Add Lines in the first browser.
8. Press Add Lines in the second browser.
9. Check only one set of lines is added and the second browser is told where the lines went.

cases.case_title: The summary card, counts per verdict, and the section review
cases.why: The findings list now shows one entry per flagged row with all its flagged positions, instead of one entry per flagged position.
steps_before: 1. Read the summary card: completion line, a count per verdict, and the findings list naming each flagged position as field, axle, row and position with its reading.
expected_before: The screen leads with a summary card: the completion line, a count per verdict, and a findings list naming each flagged position (field, axle, row, position) with the reading that earned it.
expected_now: The findings list has one entry per flagged measurement row, not one entry per flagged tire or brake.

Each entry names the field, the axle and the row, followed by every flagged position on that row with its reading, for example 'Brake & tire measurements · Axle 1 · Tire pressure: left outer 42 psi, right outer 40 psi'.
A flagged checkbox field is its own entry.
steps_now: 1. Add a Per axle field to the template next to the checkbox fields.
2. While filling, on Axle 1 Tire pressure, flag two positions (for example left outer 42 psi and right outer 40 psi, Not OK).
3. Complete the inspection and open its completed screen.
4. Read the findings list on the summary card.
5. Check the two flagged tires appear in one entry for Axle 1 · Tire pressure, listing both positions with their readings.
6. Check each flagged checkbox field appears as its own entry.

cases.case_title: Building lines when the work order is deleted, built twice, or reopened
cases.why: With its work order deleted the inspection can no longer be built from at all, and a build by someone else is no longer followed by a 'build again?' confirmation because an inspection is built from once.
steps_before: 1. Delete the run-on work order, then open the completed inspection; confirm only 'create a new work order' is offered.

2. In a second browser signed in as another user, build from the same inspection while this screen is still open in the first; check the re-build confirmation reflects the current state, not the state when the screen loaded.
expected_before: If the run-on work order has been deleted, only the option to create a new work order is offered.
If another user builds from the same inspection while this screen is open, the re-build confirmation is based on the current state rather than the state when the screen loaded.
expected_now: With the run-on work order deleted, the completed inspection offers no build action at all: no Build lines and no new-work-order option.
Its footer offers View PDF only, with or without ShopCoach: no Go to work order and no line about the work order note feed.
If lines had been built onto another work order that still exists before the deletion, the footer also shows that outcome (for example 'WO created S-235'), linking to it.

If another user adds lines from the same inspection while your screen is open, the check uses the inspection as it is now: nothing is added a second time and you are told where the lines went. No confirmation to build again appears.
After that, the screen no longer offers Build lines; its footer shows the outcome ('WO created …' or 'Lines added …') with a link.
steps_now: 1. Delete the run-on work order.
2. Open the completed inspection.
3. Check there is no build action and the footer offers View PDF only.
4. On another completed inspection with findings, open its completed screen in the first browser.
5. In the second browser, signed in as another user, build from the same inspection and press Add Lines.
6. In the first browser, without reloading, press Build lines, choose a target and, if proposed lines appear, press Add Lines.
7. Check nothing is added and you are told where the lines went.
8. Reload the completed screen.
9. Check the footer shows the outcome with a link instead of Build lines.

cases.case_title: Building again asks to confirm, based on the inspection as it is now
cases.why: Building again from the note with a confirmation is gone: once built from anywhere, the note shows the outcome instead of Build lines.
steps_before: 1. From the note, press Build lines on an inspection that has already been built from elsewhere.
2. Confirm the confirmation prompt is based on the inspection's current state rather than on the note's snapshot.
expected_before: The re-build confirmation is based on the inspection's current state rather than on the note, so a build done elsewhere afterwards still triggers the warning.
If the inspection was already built from through another entry point, the user is asked to confirm.
expected_now: The note of an inspection already built from elsewhere does not offer Build lines. In its place it shows the outcome, 'WO created …' or 'Lines added …', linking to the work order that got the lines.
The note shows the inspection as it is now, even though the note was posted before the build.

If the proposed lines from the note were already open when the other build happened, pressing Add Lines adds nothing and says where the lines went.

2. Open the work order's Notes tab and find the inspection report note.

cases.case_title: The note's Build lines is hidden until the inspection is ready
cases.why: A deleted inspection's note is now marked 'Inspection deleted' and the inspection leaves the asset's Inspections tab, which the case does not check.
steps_before: 2. On a note whose inspection was deleted, confirm the note remains as a record but the action is gone.
expected_before: If the inspection has been deleted, the note remains as a record but the action is not shown.
expected_now: Removing a completed inspection from its line, or deleting the line, deletes the inspection.
Its report note stays on the work order, marked 'Inspection deleted', with no Build lines.
View PDF and Download on that note are disabled and the card is greyed out (stated by the developer in Jira; the spec only says the note is marked).
The deleted inspection no longer appears on the asset's Inspections tab.
steps_now: 1. Complete an inspection on a work order line.
2. On the Lines tab, remove the completed inspection from its line and confirm Remove.
3. Open the Notes tab and find the inspection report note.
4. Check the note is still there, marked 'Inspection deleted', with no Build lines.
5. Check View PDF and Download on the note are disabled.
6. Open the asset's Inspections tab.
7. Check the deleted inspection is not listed.

cases.why: The filter row was removed (three columns sort instead), the summary line has new words, and older inspections are simply listed with their issues rather than found under a With issues filter.
steps_before: 1. Read the filter row (All, Needs action, With issues, Not started) and confirm each count is taken from the full list, not the filtered view.
2. Read the summary 'N of M need a work order'.

3. Confirm an inspection shows Needs action only when it was completed after this release, has a Monitor or Not OK finding, and has not been built from; a pre-release inspection is never flagged but stays reachable under With issues.
expected_before: A filter row offers All, Needs action, With issues and Not started, each count taken from the full list rather than the filtered view.
A summary reads "N of M need a work order".

An inspection needs action when it was completed after this release, has at least one Monitor or Not OK finding, and has not been built from; a pre-release inspection is never flagged but stays reachable under With issues.
expected_now: The tab has no filter row: no All, Needs action, With issues or Not started.
The Inspection, Status and Completed columns can be sorted. By default the most recently completed inspection comes first.
The summary reads "N of M have findings with no lines yet".

An inspection needs action only when it was completed after this release, has a Monitor or Not OK finding and has not been built from. A pre-release inspection is never flagged; it stays listed on the tab with its issues shown.
steps_now: 1. Open the asset's Inspections tab.
2. Check there is no filter row.
3. Click the Inspection column header and check the list sorts.
4. Click the Status column header and check the list sorts.
5. Click the Completed column header and check the list sorts.
6. Reload the tab and check the most recently completed inspection is first.
7. Read the summary line and check it reads 'N of M have findings with no lines yet' with the right numbers.
8. Check only the post-release inspection with a finding that has not been built from offers the build action.
9. Check the pre-release inspection with issues is listed with its issues shown and no build action.

cases.case_title: Inspections tab links and buttons, phone use, and the inspection's asset
cases.why: The tab no longer has a filter row, and it now follows a work order when its asset is changed or assets are merged, instead of staying on the asset first inspected.
steps_before: 2. On a phone, confirm every column's information stays reachable and the page does not scroll sideways; the filter row wraps and keeps its counts.

3. Confirm the tab shows what was inspected (asset stored on the inspection at creation), not a view that follows a later work-order asset change; confirm a pre-release inspection was backfilled from its work order's asset.
expected_before: The filter row wraps on a phone rather than scrolling out of view, and keeps its counts.

An inspection records the asset it was run on, stored on the inspection at creation rather than derived through its work order, and pre-release inspections are backfilled from their work order's asset at migration.
expected_now: There is no filter row on the tab, so there is nothing to wrap on a phone; every column's information stays reachable and the page does not scroll sideways.
The tab lists the inspections whose work order is on this asset now. When a work order's asset is changed, its inspections move to the new asset's Inspections tab and leave the old one.
When two assets are merged, the inspections move to the surviving asset, as the work orders do.
Inspections from before the release are listed on their work order's asset.
steps_now: 1. On a phone, open the asset's Inspections tab.
2. Check every column's information is reachable and the page does not scroll sideways.
3. On desktop, open the work order of one inspection and change its asset to another asset.
4. Open the new asset's Inspections tab and check the inspection is listed there.
5. Open the old asset's Inspections tab and check the inspection is no longer listed.
6. Merge two assets of the same customer (for example by editing one asset's VIN to the other's and answering Yes to merge).
7. Check the inspections of both are listed on the surviving asset.
8. Check a pre-release inspection is listed on its work order's asset.

cases.case_title: How findings are counted, once per axle

steps_before: 4. Confirm the asset list, report summary and Needs action filter all follow this same count.
cases.expected_before_note: The case's Expected results have no line for step 4; the old expectation is in the step itself.
expected_now: There is no Needs action filter on the asset's Inspections tab.
The asset list, the report summary and the summary line on the tab ('N of M have findings with no lines yet') all follow the same counting.
steps_now: 1. Open the asset's Inspections tab for these inspections.
2. Check each row's findings match the counts from steps 1 to 3.
3. Open each inspection's report and check its summary shows the same counts.
4. Check the summary line 'N of M have findings with no lines yet' agrees with these inspections.

cases.case_title: Inspections tab with not-started, all N/A, deleted, moved and many inspections
cases.why: After the run-on work order is deleted, only an inspection with a report is kept, as a read-only record that can no longer be built from, reopened or regenerated.
steps_before: 3. Delete the run-on work order and confirm the inspection stays listed with a dash in the work order column and remains usable; delete a different work order the lines were built onto and confirm the row returns to Needs action.
expected_before: If the run-on work order has been deleted, the inspection stays listed, the work order column shows a dash rather than a broken link, and the row stays usable.
expected_now: Only an inspection that has a report (completed, or reopened after completing) stays listed after its work order is deleted. One with no report (not finished, or submitted without its report being generated) is deleted with the work order.

The kept row is a read-only record with a dash in the Work order column. It can be opened and its latest report downloaded, but it cannot be built from, reopened or regenerated; its completed screen offers View PDF only.
The Action column shows the outcome only while the work order it points to still exists (for example 'WO created S-200' when the lines went onto another work order); otherwise it shows a dash.
A reopened inspection shows Status 'Completed' with the date of its latest report, and opening the row opens that report rather than the answers.
steps_now: 1. On one work order for this asset, complete one inspection, complete and then reopen a second, and leave a third unfinished.
2. Delete the work order.
3. Open the asset's Inspections tab.
4. Check the completed and the reopened inspections are listed with a dash in Work order, and the unfinished one is gone.
5. Check the reopened one reads Completed with the date of its latest report.
6. Open the completed one and check it is read-only and offers View PDF only (no Build lines, no Reopen).
7. Open the reopened one's row and check its latest report opens.
8. For an inspection whose lines went onto another work order before its own work order was deleted, check the Action column shows 'WO created …' linking to that work order.
